ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a titration curve, with the vertical axis as pH and the horizontal axis as Volume NaOH (mL). The curve has two obvious rising regions, of which the second, steeper equivalence point is located near about 20 mL NaOH. Reasoning: According to the method draft, take the second equivalence point as 20 mL NaOH. The NaOH concentration is 0.10 M, so the amount of substance of NaOH added at the second equivalence point is 0.10 mol/L × 0.020 L = 0.0020 mol. H2C2O4 is a diprotic acid, and complete neutralization of 1 mol H2C2O4 requires 2 mol NaOH, so the amount of substance of H2C2O4 is 0.0020/2 = 0.0010 mol. The initial acid solution volume is 20 mL = 0.020 L, so the concentration is 0.0010 mol / 0.020 L = 0.050 M.

A 0.10 M solution of NaOH is titrated into 20 mL of $H_2C_2O_4$, a diprotic acid, of an unknown concentration. The pH of the $H_2C_2O_4$ solution is monitored as the NaOH is added, resulting in the graph below.

method.method_draft: From the graph, identify the second equivalence point at approximately 20 mL NaOH. Use the text-given NaOH concentration, 0.10 M, to compute moles NaOH: 0.10 mol/L × 0.020 L = 0.0020 mol NaOH. Since H2C2O4 is diprotic, moles acid = 0.0020/2 = 0.0010 mol. Divide by the initial acid volume from the text, 20 mL = 0.020 L, giving [H2C2O4] = 0.0010/0.020 = 0.050 M.
